Prioritization is `the act or process of arranging tasks, goals, or items in order of relative importance and urgency`.[[1]](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/us/dictionary/english/prioritization)[[2]](https://www.vocabulary.com/dictionary/prioritization)

### Definition & Purpose

- **Core Goal:** Helps individuals and teams direct limited time, money, and focus toward high-impact activities while reducing stress and burnout.
- **Application:** Used across daily personal task management, business project management, software development backlogs, and clinical medical evaluations.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prioritization)[[2]](https://www.mindtools.com/adwtc03/prioritization/)[[3]](https://www.coursera.org/articles/how-to-prioritize-tasks)[[4]](https://www.vocabulary.com/dictionary/prioritization)[[5]](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/us/dictionary/english/prioritization)

### Common Prioritization Methods

- **Eisenhower Matrix:** Divides tasks into four quadrants based on urgency and importance (Do, Schedule, Delegate, Eliminate).
- **ABCDE Method:** Ranks tasks from A (must do) to E (eliminate).
- **MoSCoW Method:** Categorizes requirements into Must have, Should have, Could have, and Won't have.
- **RICE Scoring:** Evaluates projects using Reach, Impact, Confidence, and Effort.
- **Ivy Lee Method:** Write down your top six tasks each day and order them by true importance, working through them one by one.[[1]](https://www.dalecarnegie.com/blog/prioritize-prioritization-how-to-help-employees-decide-where-to-start/)[[2]](https://www.meistertask.com/blog/10-powerful-task-prioritization-methods)[[3]](https://www.indeed.com/career-advice/career-development/prioritization-strategies)

You can learn more about structured approaches on [Mind Tools](https://www.mindtools.com/adwtc03/prioritization/) or explore step-by-step career strategies via [Indeed's Guide to Prioritization](https://www.indeed.com/career-advice/career-development/prioritization-strategies).If you'd like, tell me:

- Are you prioritizing **personal daily tasks** or a **work/project management** workload?
- What is the **main challenge** you are facing right now (e.g., too many deadlines, feeling overwhelmed, or unclear goals)?

I can recommend the best framework and walk you through setting it up.
